title: Hubble revisits tangled NGC 6240
caption: The merging galaxy NGC 6240, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 6240 · constellation Ophiuchus · about 400 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration, and A. Evans (University of Virginia, Charlottesville/NRAO/Stony Brook University)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A tangle of gas, dust and stars spreads out in branching wisps, loops and tails, with a knotted, pinky-red region at its center. This is NGC 6240, 400 million light-years away in the constellation Ophiuchus. Its shape has been compared to a butterfly and, less flatteringly, to a lobster.

The galaxy did not start out like this. Its twisted form is the result of two galaxies drifting too close and merging. That collision set off bursts of star formation, and many of the hot young stars it produced have since exploded as supernovae. One, named SN 2013dc, was discovered in 2013. It does not appear in this image, though its position is marked.

At the heart of the jumble, the two galaxies' central supermassive black holes are spiralling toward each other. They are only some 3000 light-years apart, very close for a galaxy that spans 300 000 light-years, and are expected to merge into a single immense black hole.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.89 x 2.89 arcminutes) and distance (400 million light years), the frame spans roughly 336,000 × 336,000 light-years. Its light set out about 400 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines visible, near-infrared and hydrogen-alpha observations from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and Wide Field Camera 3. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: The galaxy is far too distant and faint to see like this by eye, and part of the data comes from near-infrared light that the eye cannot detect.

explore: Hubble released an earlier image of NGC 6240 in 2008. The knotted central region seen here in pinky-red was only revealed by these newer observations from Wide Field Camera 3 and the Advanced Camera for Surveys.
alt: An irregular, tangled galaxy with branching wisps, loops and tails of gas, dust and stars and a knotted pinky-red center.
